title: Mutual effort
caption: if you're the only one moving, it's not an orbit. it's a chase

lines: You've been told the moon orbits the *earth.*
That's only half of it.
They both circle a *point* between them,
so the earth *wobbles* a little every month.
That's what real love looks like.
Not one person holding *still*
while the other does all the moving.
Both of you get pulled. Both of you *give.*
Say it with me.
I don't do all the *moving* anymore.
I want love that pulls *both* ways.
I meet effort with effort.

title: Being chosen
caption: saturn collects moons. earth keeps one, close enough to move the sea

lines: Saturn has more than two hundred *moons.*
Most of them are tiny.
Earth has *one.*
And it holds that one close enough
to move every *ocean* on the planet.
You weren't made to be one of *hundreds.*
You were made to be *chosen,*
clearly, and on purpose.
Say it with me.
I am nobody's *backup* option.
I want to be someone's *one,*
and to know it without asking.

title: Consistency over intensity
caption: a shooting star is a speck of dust having a moment. the sun just shows up

lines: Most shooting stars are a speck of *dust.*
One bright second, and it's gone.
It feels like magic because it's *brief.*
The sun is never that *dramatic.*
It just comes up again tomorrow,
and the morning after that.
That's the light that keeps you *warm.*
Choose the steady one over the *flash.*
Say it with me.
I don't confuse intensity with *love.*
I want someone who shows up *again.*
Steady feels like *home* to me.

title: Slow love
caption: the full moon takes two weeks and nobody calls it slow

lines: The full moon takes about two weeks to *build.*
Dark to full, a sliver at a time,
and it doesn't skip a single night.
And no one looks up and calls it *slow.*
They call it *full.*
If love is building slowly with someone,
that isn't a lack of *spark.*
It's a light that's *staying.*
Say it with me.
I don't have to rush to be *sure.*
Slow is how I *build* things that last.

title: The closure you give yourself
caption: you can stop waiting for the message. the light already sent everything it had

lines: Starlight is always *old* news.
Some of what you see tonight
left its star *centuries* ago.
You're seeing what it *was,*
not what it is now.
So you can stop waiting for a final *answer*
from someone who already *left.*
Their light is all they were ever going to send.
*Closure* is something you can give yourself.
Say it with me.
I don't need their *words* to move on.
I already know what *happened.*
I give myself the *ending.*

title: Being ghosted
caption: space is silent because nothing's there to carry the sound. you don't have to decode it

lines: Space is completely *silent.*
Sound needs air to travel through,
and out there, there's *nothing* to carry it.
So when someone goes quiet on you,
the silence isn't a *code* to crack.
It's just empty space
where a *reply* should have been.
That's an *answer* too.
Say it with me.
I don't chase people into the *dark.*
Their silence is not my *worth.*
I deserve someone who *answers.*

title: Mixed signals
caption: stars flicker through rough air. planets shine steady. look for the steady ones

lines: A twinkle is just *turbulence.*
Starlight gets shaken by rough air
on its way down to *you.*
Planets mostly don't twinkle. They shine *steady.*
If someone's light keeps *flickering,*
warm one day, gone the next,
you don't have to *decode* it.
Mixed signals are a *signal.*
They mean someone isn't sure.
Say it with me.
I don't squint to see someone's *interest.*
I want love that shines *steady.*
Clear is *kind,* and I deserve clear.

title: Waiting for a text
caption: sunlight crosses ninety-three million miles in eight minutes. a reply can cross a room

lines: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to reach you.
It crosses ninety-three million *miles,*
and it still finds you, every *morning.*
So if you've been staring at your phone
for a reply that's taking *days,*
it isn't the *distance.*
People who want to reach you find a way.
Say it with me.
I don't wait by the phone for *proof.*
I deserve someone who *replies*
like they're glad I wrote.

title: Overthinking
caption: mercury laps the sun every eighty-eight days. no wonder your thoughts lap themselves

lines: The planet of your mind is the *fastest* one.
Mercury circles the sun in eighty-eight days.
No wonder your thoughts *lap* themselves.
A few times a year, it even looks
like it's going *backwards,*
replaying the same stretch of sky.
That's what overthinking feels like.
The same text, read a *hundred* times.
Say it with me.
I don't have to solve love *tonight.*
My thoughts can loop. I don't have to *follow.*
What's meant for me won't be a *riddle.*

title: Jealousy
caption: venus is hotter than mercury. not because it's closer, because the heat can't get out

lines: You'd think the hottest planet is *Mercury.*
It's the closest to the sun.
It isn't. The hottest is *Venus,*
the planet of love.

scenes.header: VENUS · HEAT WITH NOWHERE TO GO
lines: Its thick air *traps* the heat in,
with nowhere for it to go.
Jealousy works the *same* way.
A feeling with no way out
just keeps *burning.*
Let it out as words, not as *watching.*
Say it with me.
I can feel jealous and still be *kind.*
I say what I'm afraid of, out *loud.*

title: Comparing yourself
caption: on venus the sun rises in the west. still the brightest planet in our sky

lines: On Venus, the sun rises in the *west.*
It spins the opposite way to most planets,
and slower than any of them.
And it's still the *brightest* planet in our sky.
It never had to turn like the others
to *shine.*
You don't either.
Say it with me.
I don't measure my light by *theirs.*
I'm allowed to *turn* my own way.
The way I spin is *mine.*

title: Loving yourself first
caption: nobody lights a star. it pulls itself together first, then it shines

lines: Nobody lights a *star.*
It starts as a cold, dark *cloud,*
and its own gravity pulls it together,
tighter and hotter, until it *lights.*
Loving yourself first is like that.
Gathering yourself *before* you give yourself away,
so what someone else brings is *warmth,*
not the only *light* you have.
Say it with me.
I am my own first *light.*
Love adds to me. It doesn't *start* me.

title: Boundaries
caption: earth's magnetic field turns the solar wind away. what gets through becomes the northern lights

lines: Earth wears an invisible *shield.*
It's the magnetic field,
and it turns away a wind from the sun
that never stops *blowing.*
What slips through, near the poles,
becomes the northern *lights.*
A boundary isn't a *wall.*
It's what turns a storm into something beautiful.
Say it with me.
My boundaries are not *cold.*
They're how I stay *close*
without getting burned.

title: Saying the honest thing
caption: the full moon is just the moon facing the sun straight on. that's all honesty is

lines: A full moon hides *nothing.*
It's the moon facing the sun straight on,
every crater *showing.*
That's what saying the honest thing feels like.
*Exposed.* Like everyone can see the craters.
But it's the only night
the moon gets seen *whole.*
Say it with me.
I say what I *mean,* gently.
The right person can hold my *truth.*
I'd rather be seen than stay *hidden.*

title: Dealbreakers up front
caption: saturn's rings stay sharp because tiny moons guard the edges. say your dealbreakers early

lines: Look closely at Saturn's *rings.*
Some of their edges are razor-sharp,
held in place by tiny moons
called *shepherd* moons.
Dealbreakers work like that.
Saying what you won't accept, up *front,*
isn't cold or *picky.*
It's what keeps something beautiful
from *scattering* later.
Say it with me.
I name my *dealbreakers* early.
The right person won't *flinch.*
Clear edges keep my love in *shape.*

title: Red flags you explained away
caption: mars is red because its dust is rusting, and you can tell from your backyard

lines: You can see Mars is red from your *backyard.*
No telescope. Millions of miles away.
Its dust is full of *rust.*
Some things are red from a *distance.*
You saw it early. You explained it.
That wasn't you being *foolish.*
That was you *hoping.*
Say it with me.
When I see *red,* I believe it.
I don't need to get *closer* to check.
My hope is safe with *me.*

title: Green flags
caption: the green flash is real. you just have to be watching a calm horizon

lines: Right as the sun slips under a clear horizon,
there's sometimes a *green* flash.
It lasts a second or two.
It's real. Most people *miss* it.
Green flags are like that.
They don't *announce* themselves.
They show up in calm, ordinary *moments,*
if you're not too busy watching for *storms.*
Say it with me.
I notice the *quiet* good things.
Calm is not *boring* to me.

title: The person who stays
caption: the north star isn't the brightest. it's the one that doesn't move

lines: The North Star isn't the *brightest* star.
Dozens of stars outshine it.
It's famous for one thing:
it *stays.*
The whole sky turns around it all night,
and it barely *moves.*
Sailors steered home by it for centuries.
The person who stays won't always be
the *brightest* thing in the room.
Say it with me.
I choose people who *stay.*
I can be the one who stays, *too.*

title: Peace over chaos
caption: jupiter's great red spot has been spinning for a century and a half. still just spinning

lines: Jupiter has a storm wider than the *earth.*
People have watched it spin
for more than a century and a *half.*
Huge, wild, and still just *spinning.*
Chaos can feel like *depth.*
All that spinning feels like *passion.*
But love that's right for you
feels more like a clear *night*
than a storm you have to survive.
Say it with me.
I choose *peace* over chaos.
Calm love is still *real* love.

title: Not chasing
caption: the sun has never once gone after a planet. it keeps burning, and they stay

lines: The sun has never chased a single *planet.*
It just keeps *burning,*
and eight of them stay in orbit.
Not chasing isn't playing *cold.*
It's staying lit where you are,
and letting the ones who want your warmth
come *closer* on their own.
Say it with me.
I don't run after *anyone.*
The right people find their way to my *light.*
I stay warm. I stay *here.*

title: Learning to receive love
caption: the moon doesn't make light. it's just very good at letting it land

lines: Moonlight is just sunlight, *received.*
The moon makes no light of its own.
It just lets the sun's light *land.*
And it lights up the whole *night* with it.
If being given love makes you *flinch,*
if you rush to pay it back,
remember the moon.
*Receiving* is how it shines.
Say it with me.
I let love *land.*
I don't have to earn every kind *thing.*

title: Feeling like too much
caption: a million earths would fit inside the sun. nobody asks it to shrink

lines: You could fit a million Earths inside the *sun.*
Nobody calls it *too much.*
They call it the reason anything *grows.*
If someone told you you were too much,
maybe they wanted a *candle.*
You don't have to *dim.*
The right people find the right distance
and get *warm.*
Say it with me.
I am not too much. I am *whole.*
I don't shrink to be *loved.*

title: Being enough
caption: the moon is four hundred times smaller than the sun and still covers it perfectly

lines: From here, the moon and sun look the same *size.*
The moon is four hundred times *smaller,*
but about four hundred times *closer.*
So in a total eclipse, it fits just right.
Not by being *bigger.*
By being *exactly* where it is.
You don't have to grow to be enough.
You already *fit.*
Say it with me.
I am enough at my real *size.*
I don't have to be more to be *chosen.*

title: Choosing yourself
caption: pluto got demoted in two thousand six. turns out it had a heart on it the whole time

lines: In two thousand six, Pluto lost its *title.*
Overnight, it wasn't a planet anymore.
Pluto didn't change one *bit.*
Nine years later, a spacecraft flew past it
and found a *heart* on its surface,
about a thousand miles wide.
Someone else's label never changed what you *are.*

scenes.header: FIRST HOUSE · SAY IT WITH ME
lines: Say it with me.
I can be left off someone's list
and still be *whole.*
I choose myself, *heart* and all.

title: Starting over
caption: the moon goes completely dark every month and nobody calls it a failure

lines: Every month, the moon goes completely *dark.*
And no one thinks the moon has *failed.*
It's called the *new* moon.
It's literally phase one.
Starting over in love works the same way.
It feels like losing *everything* you built.
It's really the sky making room
for the next *light.*
Say it with me.
I'm not starting from *nothing.*
I'm starting from *new.*
My next light is already on its way.

title: A new deal at eleven eleven
caption: the sky at eleven eleven tonight has never existed before. neither has your next chance

lines: At eleven eleven tonight, the sky will be
in a shape it has never been in *before.*
Since last night, the moon alone has moved
about *thirteen* degrees.
Every night, the sky gets *dealt* again.
Whatever hand you got in love *yesterday,*
it isn't the only one *coming.*
Say it with me.
My yesterday doesn't decide *tonight.*
I'm ready for a new *hand.*
I make my wish, and I keep my *eyes* open.

title: You won't arrive alone
caption: a lot of what looks like one star is two. you just can't tell from here

lines: A lot of what looks like one *star*
is actually two, circling each other.
From this far away, you can't *tell.*
Most stars are born in *groups,*
from the same cloud. Even the sun
probably had *siblings.*
You won't arrive alone, *either.*
The people who'll love you
are already out there, *moving.*
Say it with me.
I'm not as alone as I *look* from here.
Someone out there is looking *up* too.

title: Read the sky before the face
caption: people crossed the pacific by reading the stars. a face is just the surface

lines: People once crossed the Pacific in *canoes,*
steering by where the stars *rose* and set.
No maps. Just the sky, read *closely.*

scenes.header: READ THE SKY · THEN THE FACE
lines: A face is only the *surface.*
It shows you what someone looks like.
Their sky says how they *love,*
how they fight, how they stay.
Say it with me.
I look *deeper* than a face.
I want someone whose sky *fits* mine.

title: Release, don't haunt
caption: the waning moon gives its light back one night at a time and never looks over its shoulder

lines: A waning moon lets go a little *every* night.
It doesn't cling to the light it *had.*
It gets quieter, until it's *new.*
When you let someone go,
let them go *all* the way.
Don't hover at the edge of their sky,
checking their stories from the *dark.*
A ghost can't start *over.*
Say it with me.
I release what's gone, *completely.*
I don't haunt the people I let go.
My energy comes *home* to me.

title: Timing
caption: there's a new moon every month. an eclipse only a few times a year. timing is everything

scenes.header: NEW MOON · JUST OFF THE LINE
lines: A new moon happens every *month.*
So why isn't there an eclipse every month?
Because the moon's path is *tilted,* just a little.
Most months, it slips just *above* or below.
Only a few times a year, it lines up *exactly.*
And that's an *eclipse.*
If love hasn't lined up yet,
it doesn't mean something's *wrong* with you.
Sometimes the paths just aren't there yet.
Say it with me.
My timing is not a *verdict* on me.
I trust the *slow* math of the sky.

title: Patience
caption: jupiter takes twelve years to go around once. it gets to every part of your chart eventually

lines: The planet of luck is in no *hurry.*
Jupiter takes twelve years to circle the sun,
about a *year* in every sign.
It moves through every house of your *chart,*
your house of *partners* too.
If love feels late, it isn't *lost.*
It's on a long road, and it's moving.
Say it with me.
I'm not *behind.* I'm on my way.
Good things can take the long *road* to me.

title: When it ends anyway
caption: in a lunar eclipse the moon doesn't go black. it turns red, lit by every sunset on earth

lines: In a lunar eclipse, the moon doesn't go *black.*
It turns *red.*
That red is sunlight bending through our air,
every sunrise and sunset on *earth*
landing on it at once.
When love ends anyway, after you *tried,*
you don't go dark either.
You just get lit in a way
you didn't *expect.*
Say it with me.
I gave it my *all,* and it still ended.
I'm still *lit.*
This isn't the end of my *light.*

title: Letting love be easy
caption: nothing in orbit is trying to stay up. it's falling the right way

lines: Nothing in orbit is *trying* to stay up.
A planet is just falling toward the sun,
moving fast enough to keep *missing.*
No engine. Just the right *path.*
Love isn't always effortless.
But when it's right, you don't *fight*
just to keep it in the *sky.*
Easy isn't *boring.*
Easy is two people on the same path.
Say it with me.
I'm allowed to have love that's *easy.*
I stop mistaking a *struggle* for proof.

title: Being someone's first choice
caption: venus shows up before the stars do. being someone's first choice should look like that

lines: Before a single star comes out, there's *Venus.*
For months at a time, it's the evening *star,*
the first light you see after sunset.
You never have to search the sky for it.
Being someone's first choice feels like that.
*Obvious.* Not something you have to guess at,
or wait until everyone else has *left.*
Say it with me.
I want to be someone's *first* light,
not the one they *settle* for.
I never have to *wonder* where I stand.

title: Forgiveness
caption: the moon keeps every crater. the earth has rain and wind, so its marks soften

lines: The moon never forgets a *hit.*
Its craters last for billions of years,
with no wind or rain to *soften* them.
The earth gets hit too.
But rain, wind and time wear its *marks* down.
That's what *forgiveness* can be.
Not saying it didn't hit you.
Just letting weather move through,
so it stops being the *only* thing you see.
Say it with me.
I can forgive and still *remember.*
I let time soften what *hurt* me.

title: Missing someone
caption: the moon drifts about four centimeters further every year and still moves the tides

lines: The moon is leaving us, very *slowly.*
About four *centimeters* every year.
And it still moves the tides, every day.
Missing someone works like that.
The distance grows, and the *pull*
doesn't get the *message* right away.
Missing them isn't a sign to go *back.*
It's just gravity catching up.
Say it with me.
I can *miss* someone and still let go.
The tide comes in. The tide goes *out.*
And I keep walking *forward.*

title: Going no contact
caption: every two years mars slips behind the sun and mission teams stop messaging it. on purpose

lines: Every two years or so, Mars slips behind the *sun.*
And the teams who run its rovers
stop sending them *messages.*
On *purpose.*
Anything sent past the sun gets *scrambled,*
so they wait it out.
Going no contact is that.
Not cruel. Just knowing which messages
can't get through *right* now.
Say it with me.
I don't owe the past a *reply.*
My silence is *care,* not cruelty.
I'm protecting my *peace.*

title: The ex who comes back
caption: a comet comes back glowing because the sun is heating it, not because its orbit changed

lines: A comet swings back toward the sun,
*blazing,* with a tail across the sky.
Then it leaves again for *years.*
That glow isn't change.
It's ice turning to *gas* in the heat.
So when an ex comes back shining,
ask if the *orbit* changed,
or just the light.
Say it with me.
I don't mistake a *return* for a change.
I don't rearrange my sky for a *visit.*

title: Getting your hopes up
cover: Let it rise to its *real* size
caption: the moon looks huge on the horizon. it isn't any bigger. your brain just gets excited

lines: You know how the moon looks *huge* on the horizon?
It isn't any bigger.
It's the same moon, the same size.
Your brain is doing that, not the *sky.*

scenes.header: HIGH IN THE SKY · TRUE SIZE
lines: Hope does that to the first few *messages.*
Getting your hopes up isn't *foolish.*
Just let things *rise,*
and show their real size as they climb.
Say it with me.
I can hope and still see *clearly.*
I let people show me who they *are.*

title: First date nerves
caption: the solid ground under you rises a little when the moon goes over. nerves are just a tide

lines: The ground under your *feet* moves with the moon.
Not just the ocean. The actual rock
*lifts* a little, twice a day.
The earth isn't *nervous.*
It's just feeling something close.
That flutter before a first date
isn't a warning. It's a *tide.*
It means you *care* how this goes.
Say it with me.
My nerves just mean I'm *open.*
I don't have to be perfect to be *liked.*
I just have to show up as *me.*

title: Being vulnerable
caption: there's no dark side of the moon. just a side we haven't seen

lines: There's no dark side of the *moon.*
The far side gets just as much *sunlight.*
We just never see it,
because the moon only shows us one face.
Everyone has a side they *keep* turned away.
It isn't your *dark* side.
It's just the part nobody's seen yet.
Being vulnerable is letting *someone* look.
Say it with me.
The parts of me I *hide* are not dark.
I let the right person see all of me.
I'm *brave* enough to be seen.

title: Trusting again
caption: venus disappears into the sun's glare, then comes back as the morning star

lines: Sometimes Venus just *disappears.*
It slips into the sun's glare, out of sight.
Then it comes back as the *morning* star,
shining its brightest just before *dawn.*
Trusting again is like that.
You went quiet for a while.
That wasn't you *breaking.*
That was you getting ready to *rise.*
Say it with me.
I can open my heart *again.*
What hurt me before doesn't get to *decide.*
I'm coming back *brighter.*
